ADR-0063's second wave, first: the monthly 'Ask HN: Who is hiring?' thread, found each run among the stories of the account this slug names and read whole through Algolia's Hacker News API, two requests a run. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store. The employer is read from each post's first line.

ADR-0063's second wave, with the thread: Hacker News' job stories, Y Combinator companies' posts, the newest hundred of Algolia's job tag, one request a run. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store. The employer is read from the story's title.

ADR-0063's second wave, after Hacker News: Jobicy's public Jobs API, its whole feed, 200 a page newest first, read back to what is stored, about one page a run. Its terms: no more than one pass an hour, attribution kept, no listing shown as one's own; each row links to Jobicy's page and names it as its board. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store. The slug is a label; the feed has no account.

ADR-0063's second wave, after Jobicy: Remote OK's API, its newest postings in one request a run, about 99 over two months. Its terms: link back to the posting on Remote OK and name it as the source, or access is suspended; each row links to its Remote OK page and names it as its board. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store. The slug is a label; the feed has no account.

ADR-0063's second wave, last: We Work Remotely's all-jobs RSS, the newest ten postings of each category, one request a run, fetched as text and decoded by its adapter. Its terms: links attributed back to We Work Remotely; each row links to its page there and names it as its board. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store. The slug is a label; the feed has no account.

Research 0006 and ADR-0063's Changes of 2026-10-20: Python.org's job board, its RSS of the newest 20 postings, one request a run, fetched as text and decoded by its adapter. Its robots rules leave /jobs/ open and its Legal Statements say nothing on automated reading. The feed carries no date, so its postings are ordered after every dated one, the operator's decision of 2026-10-20. Each row links to its page on Python.org and names it as its board. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store. The slug is a label; the feed has no account.

Research 0006 and ADR-0063's Changes of 2026-10-20: Hasjob's Atom feed of its newest postings, one request a run, fetched as text and decoded by its adapter. Its terms have no clause on automated reading, and its robots rules bar only its edit, confirm, withdraw and admin pages. India-centred: a place is a city or Anywhere, with no country stated. Each row links to its page on Hasjob and names it as its board. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store. The slug is a label; the feed has no account.

Research 0006 and ADR-0063's Changes of 2026-10-20: Startup.jobs through its keyed API, never its RSS feed, which its terms forbid; the remote jobs (workplace_type=remote), about 585 a day, live jobs of the last 14 days, newest first, read back to what is stored. The key is the secret STARTUP_JOBS_API_KEY. Its postings are kept past the seven days its API terms set, the operator's decision of 2026-10-20. Each row links to its page on Startup.jobs and names it as its board. An aggregator, so its rows keep to the private store.
